history.alt_text: Densely packed intermodal shipping containers and warehouse bays viewed through a compressed telephoto lens.
history.caption: As warehousing space shrinks and air freight terms shorten, the physical buffer in supply chains is becoming exceptionally tight.
history.title: Supply Chain Capacity Squeeze

style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: A 200mm telephoto compression shot of densely stacked intermodal cargo containers towering next to a massive industrial warehouse exterior, crystal-clear distance clarity. Flat compressed perspective, sharp directional sunlight and deep industrial contrast, casting long dark shadows over the narrow remaining aisles. The stacked structures create a claustrophobic sense of constrained physical capacity, painted in weathered industrial blues and faded safety orange. No people in the foreground, no fog or haze, crisp clean high-contrast atmosphere.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, typography, watermarks, UI, people, faces, fog, haze, blurry
rationale: For a logistics story about capacity constraints and the physical reality of safety stock, long-lens telephoto compression perfectly captures the sheer scale and claustrophobic tightening of warehouse and freight space.
cue: Both legs of the buffer-versus-expedite trade stopped being priceable
subject: densely stacked intermodal containers and warehouse bays
core_thesis: Supply chain safety-stock models are breaking down as both fast shipping options and physical warehousing capacity become simultaneously constrained and unpredictable.
core_conflict: buffer versus expedite (warehousing capacity vs air freight availability)
composition: flat compressed perspective with stacked overlapping layers

caption: The Safety Stock Squeeze: Short air deals and tight storage break the safety buffer.
